settings.tagline: The GraphQL-first headless CMS in a single Rust binary
settings.description: Tess is a self-hostable, GraphQL-first headless CMS written in Rust. Define content models at runtime, publish with review workflows, and run it on Docker, a VM or AWS Lambda.
settings.footerText: © 2026 Tess Dev Team. Community edition for personal use, Enterprise edition for commercial use.

data.title: Tess vs Directus
data.description: Tess compared with Directus (Data platform over SQL databases (Node.js)): A Node.js platform that turns an existing SQL database into REST and GraphQL APIs with an admin app.

competitor.name: Directus
competitor.summary: A Node.js platform that turns an existing SQL database into REST and GraphQL APIs with an admin app.

rows.tess: Tess owns its storage and schema
rows.other: Mirrors the tables of an existing SQL database

rows.tess: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, DynamoDB, RocksDB
rows.other: SQL databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, MS SQL, Oracle, CockroachDB
Business Source License: free under a revenue threshold, commercial license above

competitor.chooseThem:
- You must expose an existing SQL database as is.
- You want built-in automation flows.
competitor.chooseTess:
- You start from content models, not from existing tables.
- You need NoSQL (MongoDB, DynamoDB) or an embedded database, or AWS Lambda.
competitor.migration: Each Directus collection becomes a Tess content type, and its relational fields become `RELATION` fields. Write them in the `tess-transfer` YAML format, import them, then copy the items through both GraphQL APIs.
